extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and members of the mathematical community evaluating/interpreting inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT) and standards for mathematical verification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principled criteria for assessing the validity, verifiability, and community-handling of advanced mathematical theories (with emphasis on Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory). Addresses when computer verification is meaningful, how to resolve misunderstandings, and what institutional/experimental evidence counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer verification meaningfulness (CmpVer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer verification of a mathematical assertion is meaningful only when it is premised on the appropriate "presumed relationship" between the computer representation and the original mathematical argument/theory; in particular it can be meaningful in routine numerical computations or finite/combinatorial frameworks but not when the central issue is confusion between logically unrelated fabricated versions of a theory and the original theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where computer verification is appropriate: routine numerical computations, manipulation of data in finite groups/simplicial complexes/finite Boolean chains. Anti-pattern: attempting to use computer verification to resolve disputes that hinge on conflating fabricated, logically unrelated versions of a theory (e.g., RCS-IUT) with the original theory — such attempts cannot yield substantive progress because the fundamental presumed relationship is invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflation with fabricated versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not confuse or treat logically unrelated, fabricated versions of a theory as equivalent to the original theory; such confusion invalidates verification attempts and undermines meaningful assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This error appears in concrete examples (e.g., fabricated versions of IUT). When such confusion is present, neither computer verification nor other superficial checks will resolve the issue; rather, one must confront the original content directly (see CfrMth) or engage experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront original mathematical content (CfrMth)
rubrics_metrics.description: To overcome misunderstandings arising from fabricated versions, one must directly study the original papers on the theory (IUTch I–IV and related expositions) or, if that is insufficient, engage in constructive mathematical dialogue with mathematicians who have a substantial, accurate understanding of the original theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended steps: study original sources, use the present paper and allied literature ([Alien], lecture notes, slides, videos), and enter into patient dialogue (often time-consuming) to make explicit the logical structure (see ExplLS). The author asserts this is the only reliable route to resolve such misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to engage via citation proliferation is unacceptable (RfsDlg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the proliferation/citation of fabricated versions as an excuse to refuse constructive mathematical dialogue is an illegitimate stance and amounts to avoiding the required mathematical engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavior is characterized as a "lame excuse" or subterfuge. The paper flags it as prevalent in some sectors and as obstructive to resolving disputes about the theory. The correct practice is to engage in dialogue and confront the original mathematics rather than hide behind citations of flawed secondary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional responsibility and infrastructural apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematical community that bears active responsibility for a theory will maintain an infrastructural apparatus (workshops, lecture series, accessible lecture notes/slides/videos, extensive one-to-one discussions, joint research projects) that supports sustained exposition and verification of the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive indicators of responsibility: multiple workshops, lecture series, widespread accessible materials, sustained researcher interactions. Lack of such infrastructure (as claimed for proponents of fabricated versions) signals a 'hit-and-run' approach and undermines credibility (see BlkAcc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic refusal creates mathematical "blackhole" (BlkAcc)
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic, institutionally endorsed refusal to confront the mathematical content of the original theory creates an artificial 'blackhole' of mathematical accountability, leading to pathologies and obstructions to normal operation of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a severe procedural critique: institutional avoidance prevents scrutiny and debate, undermines rule-of-law-like principles in scholarly practice (due process, burden of proof), and can lead to long-term damage in the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive dialogue and sifting assertions (ExplLS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolving misunderstandings typically requires painstaking sifting and analysis of an author's assertions to make precise and explicit the exact logical structure underlying those assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such dialogues are time-consuming; their productive completion has led, according to the author, to respondents recognizing their misunderstandings and conceding there is no mathematical reason to deny the theory (see MthVlTh). The process includes writing out logical dependencies, compartmentalizing arguments, and isolating 'blackbox' blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of concession after proper engagement (MthVlTh)
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructive mathematical dialogue is carried through sincerely and rationally, the typical chain of events is that the interlocutor recognizes misunderstandings and concedes that there is no mathematical reason to deny the validity of the theory (at least to the extent they can see).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functions as both a descriptive claim about outcomes of good-faith engagement and as an implicit normative standard: proper engagement should change the doubter's assessment if their objections were based on misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental reconstruction as evidence (DvpRcn)
rubrics_metrics.description: One way to witness the validity of a mathematical theory is developmental reconstruction: observing subsequent developments, algorithms, applications, or 'fruits' that ensue from the theory, which may corroborate its correctness even if original expositions are hard to parse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reconstruction algorithms in anabelian geometry, numerical results ([ExpEst]), new applications from enhanced versions of the theory. Historical analogues: evaluating ancient mathematical competence by architectural achievements or tablets (e.g., Plimpton 322). This is an auxiliary mode of validation when direct understanding is difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical-technical evolution to refine critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism grounded in solid, technically accurate understanding of historical and logical context tends to lead to substantive refinements of theory; by contrast, criticism based on ignorance yields spurious paradoxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper recalls historical episodes in which paradoxes (e.g., Grandi's series) prompted rigorous reformulation (Riemann/Lebesgue integration). Good critique should locate the technical source of objections and contribute to improved definitions/theorems rather than asserting contradictions from misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic representation and compartmentalization (SymIUT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing the essential logical structure of an argument/theory in simple symbolic terms (using basic logical operators, compartmentalizing complicated blocks into 'blackboxes') can make verification by mental computation feasible and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper asserts that a suitable symbolic representation of IUT's logical structure is simple enough to be mentally checkable in minutes once properly communicated. This relies on organizing/compartmentalizing complex theory blocks (anabelian geometry, étale theta functions) as blackboxes whose internal validity is taken as already established in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit applicability of computer checks to preserved logical relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Any automated or computer-based check must preserve the logical relationships and structural content of the original argument; mere mechanical checking of symbols without preserving the intended logical mappings can be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some disputes turn on whether two representations are legitimately related, mechanical checks that ignore the necessary semantic/presumed relationship are insufficient. The paper underscores the need to ensure the computer model precisely encodes the intended mathematical structures before relying on its verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat isomorphism as trivial redundancy in topology/category contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying isomorphic but distinct objects (e.g., endpoints of an interval) as 'redundant' can materially change mathematical structure (e.g., turning an interval into a loop) and thus invalidly alter logical relations (e.g., converting AND relations to OR relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete geometric examples show that passing from J to M (identifying subspaces) changes fundamental groups and the validity of relational statements; hence simplifications by identification must be justified, not assumed harmless. Anti-pattern: equating 'isomorphic' with 'identical' in contexts where global structure matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware changes in logical relators when simplifying (∧ vs ∨)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations that identify 'redundant copies' may change the truth of conjunctions vs disjunctions: an AND relation holding in the unreduced object can become only an OR relation in the reduced/identified object, with the AND failing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper models this explicitly with topology examples (AOL1–AOL4). This has implications when interpreting statements across quotients or identifications: logical structure may not be preserved by naive identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish behavior of functions versus differentials under gluing
rubrics_metrics.description: Gluing two copies of a coordinate function may fail to produce a well-defined global function (values disagree on glued point), while the associated differentials can glue to a well-defined global differential compatible with quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical distinction (AOD1–AOD3) illustrates that certain algebraic/differential objects behave differently under identifications; in broader theory-evaluation, one must track which invariants/gluings are preserved. Practical implication: choose the correct objects (e.g., differentials not functions) when seeking invariance under identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize qualitative difference of derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivatives (or their abstract analogues) can carry qualitatively different properties from original objects (e.g., symmetries), and proofs essentially relying on such derivatives are not redundant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: dismissing derivative-based arguments as unnecessary because function and derivative are 'essentially equivalent' via fundamental theorem of calculus. The paper gives examples showing derivatives may have symmetry or other properties that the originals lack, and such properties are legitimately exploited in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple modes of evidence (direct exposition, dialogue, developmental outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable validation of a theory may combine direct study of expositions, constructive dialogue with knowledgeable mathematicians, and observation of subsequent developments/applications; no single mode is universally decisive in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues for a pluralistic evaluation strategy: when direct understanding is elusive, developmental reconstruction and community infrastructure strengthen confidence; conversely, absence of community engagement and reproducible developments undermines claims.
